## Release — backlog-campaign v0.29.0

### ✨ What's new in v0.29.0

#### The campaign paces itself against your usage limits

- A `usage_budget` block sets a weekly target, such as 100% exactly at the weekly reset. The campaign reads the real usage %, scales how many workers it starts in each round to stay on that line, drains at a usage stop, and wakes again at the reset ([#1178](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1178), [#1202](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1202), [#1213](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1213)).
- The usage windows (5-hour, weekly) and where to read them are detected per host, so a plan with no 5-hour cap is not throttled by one ([#1225](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1225)).
- In a cloud session, `scripts/usage-probe.ts` turns a session's `rate_limit_event` into the same rate-limit cache the local statusline writes ([#1209](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1209)).
- The status page has a Usage budget panel: weekly %, reset time, workers allowed and a forecast. A reading past its max age is shown with its age and the target line, never hidden ([#1215](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1215), [#1260](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1260)).
- Several campaigns sharing one budget follow a documented manager/peer protocol ([#1214](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1214)).

#### Sleep mode

- While you are away, the campaign parks its questions for you instead of stalling on them. It asks them all in one round when you wake it, with a report of what happened in the meantime ([#1219](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1219), [#1233](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1233), [#1235](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1235)).
- On a local machine it keeps the host awake while the campaign sleeps ([#1241](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1241)).

#### The status page tells you what to do next

- A "Merge next" list orders the open PRs and names what blocks each one ([#1204](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1204), [#1211](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1211)).
- New panels: Run (route, sleep mode, coordination role), Decisions waiting for you, and PreToolUse denials per rule. Every top-level config block names the panel that shows it, and `verify` fails when one does not ([#1193](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1193), [#1234](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1234)).
- A launch summary (`bun run status --summary`) and a launch gate show what a run will do before it starts ([#1210](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1210), [#1220](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1220)).

#### Queue and forge

- `queue.json` is built from the forge adapter, not by hand. Large forge replies no longer fail the read, and an overflow fails loudly ([#1236](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1236), [#1242](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1242)).
- PR dependencies are mirrored onto the forge in both directions, and "Depends on owner/repo#N" links issues across repos ([#1205](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1205), [#1224](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1224)).
- Stacked PRs decide "parent landed" from the forge's merged state, and stack repair works on Gitea as well as GitHub ([#1166](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1166), [#1212](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1212)).

#### Red CI on the base branch is fixed once

- A failing check that is also red on the base branch is classified as trunk-red. The campaign fixes it in one base-fix PR instead of in every open PR, and parks the affected PRs until that fix lands ([#1172](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1172), [#1207](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1207)).

#### Safety hooks

- The Bash and file-write guards resolve more of the ways a shell command writes a file: `sort -o`, `uniq`, `git --output`, `yq -i`, `sed w`, interpreter one-liners, backslash-newline redirects, and linked worktrees as containment roots. A `>` inside quotes or a sed script no longer reads as a redirect ([#1182](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1182), [#1208](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1208), [#1228](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1228), [#1230](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1230), [#1232](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1232)).
- Long commands can no longer time a guard out into allowing the call, and a denial names the allowed alternative ([#1159](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1159), [#1196](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1196), [#1198](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1198), [#1203](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1203)).
- Recorded hook events redact tokens, cloud keys, URL credentials and client password variables ([#1189](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1189), [#1191](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1191), [#1194](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1194)).

#### Review

- The reviewer runs a slop test on UI diffs: values outside the project's token set (`V-UX-09`) and generic filler copy (`V-UX-10`) block the merge ([#1149](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1149)).

#### CI

- `verify` and PR lint run on GitHub-hosted runners, on the Node 24 action runtimes ([#1161](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1161), [#1256](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1256)).

#### Next release

- The behaviour e2e suite designed in ADR-053 ([#1247](https://github.com/CorentinLumineau/blackhole/pull/1247)) ships in the next release, not this one.
